video.title: How Anybody Can Start This $15k/Month Business

summary: Chris Koerner interviews Tim Mloud ('The Full-Time Flipper'), a former nurse in Muskoka, Ontario, who flips premium used couches bought on Kijiji/Facebook Marketplace in dense city neighbourhoods and resold from five storage units. He did $183k sales and ~$120k gross profit in 2023 working part-time, targeting ~$1,000 profit per couch, with video inspections, keyboard-shortcut scripts and deadline-driven sourcing. He also does $100 dump runs and sells a course. Key takeaway: position yourself to be first when sellers hit deadlines, relocate rather than rehab, and focus on high-value items.

speakers.name: Tim Mloud
speakers.description: Couch flipper in Muskoka, Ontario; former nurse; Instagram 'The Full-Time Flipper'

ideas.name: Premium used couch flipping on Facebook Marketplace
ideas.one_liner: Buy premium used couches cheaply from motivated sellers in dense city neighbourhoods, store them in storage-unit 'showrooms' in a rural market, and resell with video inspections and paid delivery.
ideas.business_model: Buy low / sell high per couch plus delivery fees
ideas.customer: Buyers: homeowners after renovations, new houses, or who wrecked a box-store couch; Sellers: people with deadlines (moves, closings, new couch arriving)
ideas.problem: Sellers need fast removal by deadline; buyers want quality without new-retail depreciation and can't transport couches
ideas.offer: Inspected premium couches (full-grain leather, Restoration Hardware, La-Z-Boy) with thorough 59-second video inspections, delivery available

pricing.notes: Currency Canadian dollars presumably (Ontario). Aims for ~$1,000 profit per transaction; occasional $650 fillers.

acquisition_channels.details: Buys on Kijiji (chronological) and Facebook Marketplace; sells mostly on Facebook (outsells Kijiji ~9:1)

acquisition_channels.details: Waitlist in phone contacts of buyers wanting specific couches

ideas.delivery: Solo operator with V6 SUV and 12x6 open trailer; five storage units as showrooms; outsources cleaning to an auto detailer ($150) and leather repair to a restoration guy.
unit_economics_claims: $20k sales/month goal; gross profit north of $10k

ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Immediate: first free couch sold for $280; $3k profit in first 2.5 weeks

acquisition.how: Sourcing messages could be scripted/VA-assisted, but marketplace messaging automation breaches platform rules; listing creation automatable.

delivery.how: Physical pickup, inspection, lifting and delivery.

uk_applicability.notes: Facebook Marketplace and Gumtree work in the UK; storage and van costs differ.

risks: Slower periods when prices aren't humble

tactics.name: Position to be first when impatience strikes
steps: Do one big weekly shop, start ~30 conversations on couches you want regardless of price
Watch notifications for price drops, description changes, pending-then-available
Ask about deadlines (move-out, closing, new couch arrival)
Look for impatience, indifference and ignorance (gifted expensive sectionals)
Green flags: couch moved to garage/foyer, new couch visible

quote.text: it's positioning myself to be first in line when impatience strikes
quote.speaker: Tim Mloud

tactics.name: Keyboard-shortcut messaging scripts
steps: Text expansion for 'Yep, here's a quick video inspection'
Batch questions: anyone scheduled? repairs/stains? help to lift? weekday morning pickup?
Pump the brakes: 'just starting to peek at options, might get back to you'
Return with a polite lowball: out-of-towner with trailer

quote.text: Keyboard shortcuts having everything so that you're not typing all day long
quote.speaker: Tim Mloud

tactics.name: Video inspection selling
steps: Film a 59-second inspection showing every flaw
Send on 'is this available?'
Buyers decide remotely and take delivery without surprises

tactics.name: Seller pitch: reliable easy pickup
steps: Offer full-price e-transfer immediately
Lift solo; husband needn't be home; pop the garage
Remind them to call you if their deadline hits

tactics.name: Inventory par levels
steps: Keep five storage units as showrooms
Drop prices when at capacity; buy when space frees
Target whales ($1,000+ profit), skip low-value items

tactics.name: Pre-sell from waitlist
steps: Keep contacts like 'W wants brown leather sectional'
Send cropped screenshot of a lined-up couch
Send driveway video inspection once acquired

warnings.warning: Don't start in debt; borrow a trailer instead of buying an $8k truck.

quote.text: don't start eight grand in debt. That's so stupid. Just borrow my trailer
quote.speaker: Tim Mloud

warnings.warning: Inspect thoroughly (smell for cat urine); prefer an empty trailer to a bad couch.
Comfort and unhumble pricing slowed sales; extra storage made him lazy on prices.

quote.text: I kind of took my foot off the gas pedal and uh didn't have enough humility in my pricing
quote.speaker: Tim Mloud

warnings.warning: Once you post a price you can't raise it.
Don't lie in negotiations; he regretted a fake 'little sister' story.

quote.text: Honesty always, always. Always
quote.speaker: Tim Mloud

warnings.warning: Fragile/heavy items (china cabinets, washers, tables) caused losses and injuries.

quote.text: I ate a loss on a washer and dryer. I hurt myself with a dining table. I smashed a hutch
quote.speaker: Tim Mloud

warnings.warning: Rehabbing couches was a bottleneck; relocate instead.

lessons.lesson: Look for the middleman who gets paid when a transaction stalls (U-Haul got paid because he lacked a truck).

quote.text: I'd lost 200 bucks for not owning a truck was the dilemma
quote.speaker: Tim Mloud

lessons.lesson: Start with free/cheap inventory to learn values safely, then take bigger bets.
Deadlines create deals; extract seller timelines.
Geographic arbitrage: buy where supply is dense and nobody has trucks, sell where supply is scarce.

quote.text: It's like an import business
quote.speaker: Tim Mloud

lessons.lesson: A business differs from a hobby by finding and smashing bottlenecks.

quote.text: that's the difference between it being a hobby and a business is just like identifying bottlenecks and smashing them
quote.speaker: Tim Mloud

lessons.lesson: Focus on high-value items (80/20): whales over volume.
Be open that you're a reseller so sellers and buyers become repeat sources.
A side gig can replace overtime without overhauling your career.
Hiring a VA for sourcing messages is the obvious next scaling step.
